'''''Ribes viburnifolium''''', is an uncommon North American species in the [[Grossulariaceae|gooseberry family]]. It is known by the common names '''Catalina currant''', '''Santa Catalina Island currant''', '''island gooseberry'''<ref name=taooy>{{cite web | url = http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=7149 | work = Calflora taxon report | publisher = University of California | location = Berkeley, CA | title =  Ribes viburnifolium: A. Gray, Catalina currant, Island gooseberry, Santa catalina island currant }}</ref> and '''evergreen currant'''.<ref name=tammy/>

==Description==
''Ribes viburnifolium'' is a perennial shrub<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center - The University of Texas at Austin|url=https://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=RIVI|access-date=2022-01-02|website=www.wildflower.org}}</ref> which grows low to the ground, extending long reddish stems horizontally. The leaves are dark green and shiny on their top surfaces, and lighter green or yellowish and leathery on the undersides. The leaves have glands which exude a sticky, citrus-scented sap.<ref name=tammy>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250065806 Flora of North America, ''Ribes viburnifolium'' A. Gray, 1882.  Evergreen or Catalina currant ]</ref><ref name=tabby/>

Clusters of deep red flowers bloom in late winter and into early spring. The plant yields small red fruits later in the spring.<ref name=tabby>Casebeer, M. (2004). ''Discover California Shrubs''. Hooker Press: Sonora, California. {{ISBN|0-9665463-1-8}}</ref><ref name=tammy/> The red fruit attracts birds. The flowers attract hummingbirds and insects.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Catalina Currant, Ribes viburnifolium|url=https://calscape.org/Ribes-viburnifolium-(Catalina-Currant)|access-date=2022-01-02|website=calscape.org}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==

=== Distribution ===
''Ribes viburnifolium'' is native to the coast of [[Baja California]] and [[Southern California]], from [[Smuggler's Gulch|Smuggler's Canyon]] in the Tijuana Hills of [[San Diego County, California|San Diego County]]<ref name="Reiser2001">{{Cite book |last=Reiser |first=Craig H. |url=https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/ceqa/JVR/AdminRecord/IncorporatedByReference/Appendices/Appendix-D---Biological-Resources-Report/Reiser%202001.pdf |title=Rare Plants of San Diego County |date=July 2001 |publisher=Aquafir Press |pages=216–217 |asin=B0006F4BAY |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220525183035/https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/ceqa/JVR/AdminRecord/IncorporatedByReference/Appendices/Appendix-D---Biological-Resources-Report/Reiser%202001.pdf |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref> to [[El Rosario, Baja California|El Rosario]] in central Baja California.<ref name="BajaChecklist2">{{Cite journal |last1=Rebman |first1=Jon P. |last2=Gibson |first2=Judy |last3=Rich |first3=Karen |date=15 November 2016 |title=Annotated Checklist of the Vascular Plants of Baja California, Mexico |url=http://sdplantatlas.org/pdffiles/BajaChecklist2016.pdf |journal=Proceedings of the San Diego Society of Natural History |publisher=[[San Diego Natural History Museum]] |volume=45 |pages=178 |via=San Diego Plant Atlas}}</ref> The probable [[Type (biology)|type]] locality is near [[Ensenada, Baja California|Ensenada]], from a 1882 collection by [[Marcus E. Jones]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Marcus E. |date=10 April 1882 |title=UC372607 |url=https://cch2.org/portal/collections/individual/index.php?occid=3239147&clid=0 |access-date=5 September 2022 |website=CCH2 |publisher=Consortium of California Herbaria}}</ref> ''R. viburnifolium'' is also present on several islands in the region, including [[Santa Catalina Island (California)|Catalina Island]] and [[Isla Todos Santos|Todos Santos]] in the [[Southern California Bight]], and [[Cedros Island]] farther to the south off of the [[El Vizcaíno Biosphere Reserve|Vizcaino]] Peninsula.<ref name="BajaChecklist2" /> A persistent population from a planting exists in [[San Clemente Canyon]], San Diego County.<ref name="Beauchamp">{{Cite book |last=Beauchamp |first=R. Mitchel |title=A Flora of San Diego County, California |publisher=Sweetwater River Press |year=1986 |isbn=0-931950-01-5 |location=National City, California |pages=170}}</ref>

=== Habitat ===
The mainland habitat of ''Ribes viburnifolium'' along the southern San Diego and northern Baja California coast consists of [[coastal sage scrub]] and [[Maritime succulent scrub|coastal succulent scrub]],<ref name="BajaChecklist2" /> with plants growing in [[Canyon|canyons]] and [[Arroyo (watercourse)|arroyos]] with partial shade near the coast.<ref name="WIGG">{{Cite book |last=Wiggins |first=Ira L. |title=Flora of Baja California |date=1980 |publisher=Stanford University Press |isbn=0-8047-1016-3 |location=Stanford, Calif. |pages=641 |oclc=6284257}}</ref> On the [[Punta Banda]], ''R. viburnifolium'' is found growing in moist, wind-swept, and foggy sage scrub and [[chaparral]].<ref name="Reiser2001" /> On Cedros Island, this species is found in the pine groves north of the Gran Cañón.<ref name="Oberbauer">{{Cite journal |last=Oberbauer |first=Thomas A. |date=1987 |editor-last=Hochberg |title=Floristic Analysis of Vegetation Communities on Isla de Cedros, Baja California, Mexico |journal=Third California Islands Symposium: Recent Advances in Research on the California Islands |publisher=Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History, Santa Barbara, CA. |pages=115–131}}</ref>

== Cultivation ==
'Evergreen currant' has become a popular plant in drought-tolerant gardens.<ref name="tabby" />
